title: Character at an index
description:
Write a function `char_at(text, index)` that returns the character of `text` at position `index`.

Covers source items 15-17 (character at index 0, the last index, and index 10) as one exercise with three test cases.
examples:
char_at('Coding For All', 0)
-> 'C'
char_at('Coding For All', -1)
-> 'l'
char_at('Coding For All', 10)
-> ' '
hints: Idea to consider: strings support indexing, just like lists
text[index] gives the single character at that position - index 0 is the first character, and negative indices count from the end, so text[-1] is always the last character regardless of length.
expected_behavior: Returns the single character at the given index.
explanation: Strings support the same indexing syntax as lists, including negative indices - text[-1] always means "the last character" without needing len(text) - 1.
